title: Heterogeneity-Aware Empowerment via Adaptive Robust Transfer
text: Heterogeneity-aware Empowerment via Adaptive Robust Transfer target-population inference. HEART tests variant–trait associations small target population (example, -represented ancestry biobank) borrows strength larger source population. assume genetic effects shared two populations. Source-specific signals inflate error rate, HEART asymptotically less powerful target-analysis.

title: Heterogeneity-Aware Empowerment via Adaptive Robust Transfer
text: variant j: Estimation decorrelation (heart_assoc()). HEART computes target-estimator β̂tar auxiliary estimator β̂aux. auxiliary estimator pooled, doubly robust (DR, using surrogate-based synthetic outcomes), source-. decorrelated target-estimator using joint sandwich covariance: β̂de = β̂aux − ρ̂ β̂tar, ρ̂ = Ĉov(β̂aux, β̂tar) / V̂ar(β̂tar). step gives asymptotically independent p-values (ptar, pde). Adaptive transfer via null decomposition (heart_test()). target null H0: βtar = 0 split H00 ∪ H01. four-group mixture model (ptar, pde) gives HEART statistic T = π̂00/(Ĉ1Ĉ2α̂1α̂2) · ptar1−α̂1 pde1−α̂2 + π̂01/(Ĉ1α̂1) · ptar1−α̂1. HEART estimates composite null distribution T data. gives per-variant HEART p-values, FDR q-values FWER-adjusted p-values.

code: library(BEDMatrix) G <- BEDMatrix("chr22.bed", simple_names = TRUE)        # rows must align with Y, D, X idx <- match(sample_ids, rownames(G))  # --- one array job: a chunk of variants --- fit_chunk <- heart_assoc(Y, G[idx, chunk_cols], D, X, aux = "pooled") saveRDS(fit_chunk, sprintf("assoc_chunk%03d.rds", chunk_id))  # --- after all jobs finish --- fit <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list.files(pattern = "^assoc_chunk"), readRDS)) res <- heart_test(fit$p_tar, fit$p_de_pooled, snp = fit$snp, alpha = 0.05)

what: Per-variant target-only, auxiliary and decorrelated estimators — heart_assoc
title: Per-variant target-only, auxiliary and decorrelated estimators — heart_assoc
text: Step 1 HEART. every variant (column G) function computes target-estimator \(\hat\beta^{tar}_j\), one auxiliary estimators \(\hat\beta^{aux}_j\) borrow information source sample, joint sandwich covariance, decorrelated estimator $$\hat\beta^{de}_j = \hat\beta^{aux}_j - \hat\rho_j \hat\beta^{tar}_j,   \qquad \hat\rho_j = \widehat{Cov}(\hat\beta^{aux}_j, \hat\beta^{tar}_j) /   \widehat{Var}(\hat\beta^{tar}_j),$$ whose Wald p-value \(p_{de,j}\) asymptotically independent target-p-value \(p_{tar,j}\). pair \((p_{tar,j}, p_{de,j})\) input heart_test().

text: data.frame one row per variant columns snp Variant identifier (column names G present). beta_tar, se_tar, p_tar Target-estimate, standard error two-sided p-value. beta_<aux>, se_<aux>, p_<aux> Auxiliary estimate(s). cov_<aux>, rho_<aux> Estimated covariance target-estimator projection coefficient. beta_de_<aux>, se_de_<aux>, p_de_<aux> Decorrelated estimate. Variants monomorphic target sample get NA; family = "binomial", variants whose logistic fits fail converge (e.g. complete separation variant rare target). attribute "aux" stores auxiliary estimators computed.

title: Per-variant target-only, auxiliary and decorrelated estimators — heart_assoc
text: estimators M-estimators working model \(E(Y | G_j, X) = \mu(\beta_0 + G_j\beta + X^\top\beta_X)\) identity link (family = "gaussian") logit link (family = "binomial"): "pooled" Regression pooled target + source sample (auxiliary estimator used main analyses HEART paper). "dr" Doubly robust (AIPW) estimator combines surrogate-based synthetic outcome Y_hat density ratio c_i (see heart_density_ratio()). Requires Y_hat c_i. "source" Source-regression. independent target-estimator, decorrelated estimator equals . Variances heteroscedasticity-robust sandwich variances; covariances estimators use joint sandwich formula shared sample. Gaussian family computations use Frisch-Waugh-Lovell representation vectorised blocks variants, cost per variant linear number covariates.

what: Decorrelated inverse-variance meta-analysis from summary statistics — heart_meta
title: Decorrelated inverse-variance meta-analysis from summary statistics — heart_meta
text: summary statistics independent target source studies available, inverse-variance meta-analytic estimator \(\hat\beta^{meta}_j = w^{tar}_j\hat\beta^{tar}_j + w^{src}_j\hat\beta^{src}_j\) can serve auxiliary estimator. two studies independent, \(\hat\rho_j = w^{tar}_j\) decorrelated estimator \(\hat\beta^{de}_j = w^{src}_j\hat\beta^{src}_j\) variance \((w^{src}_j)^2 v^{src}_j\); p-value therefore coincides source-study p-value. output can passed heart_test() p_de = p_de_meta.

what: Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic — heart_null_cdf
title: Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic — heart_null_cdf
text: Evaluates, statistic values t, global-null CDF \(F_{00}(t) = \int_0^1 G_t(q)dq\), empirical counterpart \(\hat Q(t) = J^{-1}\sum_j G_t(p_{de,j})\), reconstructed \(\hat F_{01}(t) = \{\hat Q(t) - \hat\pi_{00}F_{00}(t)\}/(\hat\pi_{01}+\hat\pi_{11})\) (truncated [0, 1] made nondecreasing \(t\) running maximum; set 0 \(\hat\pi_{01}+\hat\pi_{11} = 0\)), null numerator \(\hat N(t) = \hat\pi_{00}F_{00}(t) + \hat\pi_{01}\hat F_{01}(t)\) composite null CDF \(\hat F_0(t) = \hat N(t) / (\hat\pi_{00} + \hat\pi_{01})\), \(G_t(q) = \min\{1, (t/(\kappa_1 q^{1-\alpha_2} + \kappa_2))^{1/(1-\alpha_1)}\}\).

title: Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic — heart_null_cdf
code: heart_null_cdf(log_t, p_de, par, exact = FALSE, n_exact = 5000L, n_grid = 500L)

title: Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic — heart_null_cdf
text: log_t Values \(\log t\). p_de decorrelated p-values (used \(\hat Q\)). par Parameter list heart_statistic(), also containing pi11 (pi10, \(\pi_{11} = 1 - \pi_{00} - \pi_{01} - \pi_{10}\)). exact FALSE, \(F_{00}\) computed exactly n_exact smallest values interpolated (log-log) n_grid grid elsewhere. n_exact, n_grid See exact.

title: Composite null distribution of the HEART statistic — heart_null_cdf
text: data.frame columns log_t, F00, Q, F01, N, F0, sorted log_t.

what: Estimate the four-group proportions from a pair of p-value sequences — heart_pi_estimate
title: Estimate the four-group proportions from a pair of p-value sequences — heart_pi_estimate
text: Estimates \(\pi_{00}, \pi_{01}, \pi_{10}, \pi_{11}\) four-group model \((p_{tar,j}, p_{de,j})\), first index refers \(\beta^{tar}_j\) second \(\beta^{de}_j\) (0 = null, 1 = non-null). marginal joint null proportions estimated Storey-type ratios $$\hat\pi_{0\cdot}(\lambda) = \frac{\#\{p_{tar,j} > \lambda\}}{J(1-\lambda)},\quad       \hat\pi_{\cdot0}(\lambda) = \frac{\#\{p_{de,j} > \lambda\}}{J(1-\lambda)},\quad       \hat\pi_{00}(\lambda) = \frac{\#\{p_{tar,j} > \lambda, p_{de,j} > \lambda\}}{J(1-\lambda)^2},$$ \(\hat\pi_{01} = (\hat\pi_{0\cdot} - \hat\pi_{00}) \vee 0\) \(\hat\pi_{10} = (\hat\pi_{\cdot0} - \hat\pi_{00}) \vee 0\). marginal proportion set one one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov test reject uniformity. tuning parameter \(\lambda\) chosen among lambdas QQ-slope criterion maximum p-value (HDMT procedure Dai, Stanford LeBlanc, 2022).

title: HEART test statistic — heart_statistic
text: Computes simplified HEART statistic (\(\pi_{10}\) set zero) $$T_j = \hat\pi_{00}\hat C_1^{-1}\hat C_2^{-1}\hat\alpha_1^{-1}\hat\alpha_2^{-1}   p_{tar,j}^{1-\hat\alpha_1} p_{de,j}^{1-\hat\alpha_2} +   \hat\pi_{01}\hat C_1^{-1}\hat\alpha_1^{-1} p_{tar,j}^{1-\hat\alpha_1}.$$ Small values evidence \(H_{0,j}: \beta^{tar}_j = 0\).

what: Estimate the left-tail parameters of the alternative p-value density — heart_tail_estimate
title: Estimate the left-tail parameters of the alternative p-value density — heart_tail_estimate
text: two-group model \(f(p) = \pi_0 + (1-\pi_0) f_1(p)\) local approximation \(f_1(p) \approx C\alpha p^{\alpha-1}\) near zero, \((\alpha, C)\) solve conditional moment equations $$J^{-1}\sum_j \log(p_j) (p_j \le r) - \pi_0(r\log r - r) -       C(1-\pi_0) r^{\alpha}(\log r - \alpha^{-1}) = 0,$$ $$J^{-1}\sum_j (p_j \le r) = \pi_0 r + (1-\pi_0) C r^{\alpha},$$ closed-form solution. threshold \(r\) \(m\)-th smallest p-value \(m = \lceil k\sqrt{J}\rceil\). solutions truncated alpha_bounds C_bounds.

code: heart_tail_estimate(   p,   pi0,   k = 50,   pi0_cap = 0.996,   alpha_bounds = c(1e-05, 1 - 1e-05),   C_bounds = c(0.1, 3) )

title: Estimate the left-tail parameters of the alternative p-value density — heart_tail_estimate

title: Estimate the left-tail parameters of the alternative p-value density — heart_tail_estimate
text: Named numeric vector c(alpha = , C = , r = ).

title: HEART test: adaptive transfer via null decomposition — heart_test
text: FDR procedure rejects \(\{j: T_j \le \hat t_\alpha\}\) \(\hat t_\alpha = \sup\{t: \hat N(t)/\bar F(t) \le \alpha\}\); equivalently q_heart <= alpha. FWER procedure rejects \(\{j: \hat N(T_j) \le \alpha/J\}\); equivalently padj_fwer <= alpha. per-variant HEART p-value \(\hat F_0(T_j)\), estimated composite-null CDF evaluated observed statistic, can used e.g. Manhattan plots genome-wide threshold. parameters must estimated variants jointly; variants analysed chunks heart_assoc(), combine chunks calling heart_test().

title: HEART test: adaptive transfer via null decomposition — heart_test
code: sim <- heart_simulate(n_tar = 1500, n_src = 6000, J = 1000, seed = 1) fit <- heart_assoc(sim$Y, sim$G, sim$D, sim$X) res <- heart_test(fit$p_tar, fit$p_de_pooled, snp = fit$snp) res #> HEART: Heterogeneity-aware Empowerment via Adaptive Robust Transfer #>   tests: 1000 #>   four-group proportions: pi00 = 0.8100, pi01 = 0.0750, pi10 = 0.1150, pi11 = 0.0000 #>   tail parameters: alpha1 = 0.401, C1 = 1.014, alpha2 = 0.095, C2 = 1.020 #>   discoveries at level 0.05: FDR = 6, FWER = 2 (target-only BH = 2, Bonferroni = 0)
